scope: P1 internal-standard revision of five static poses; P2 reused unchanged

items.label: 걷기
items.prompt:
Project-standard P1 revision. IMAGE 1 is the previous action sketch to EDIT; IMAGE 2 is the P1 character master with the approved revised ROUND DOT EYES. Keep image 1's action readable, but enforce the identity, proportions and coat/marking design of image 2.
INTERNAL CHARACTER CONTINUITY RULES:
- Use the same individual on the SAME square 1254x1254 canvas, warm crayon on paper. Keep the master character's face width, muzzle/beard shape, ear length, leg thickness and torso anatomy consistent when joints change. Do not scale body parts independently or stretch the torso/neck to achieve a pose.
- Preserve the white central forehead blaze through the bridge into white muzzle/beard; gray lateral face and SHORT gray floppy ears, white neck/bib and lower paws, gray back/flank and upper-leg zones. Match the master area's boundaries as the skin surface turns; no extra cheek spots, new bands, orange patches or mirrored markings. Use only the visible side; do not turn to an unseen side or infer hidden anatomy.
- Preserve the APPROVED SMALL ROUND SOLID dark crayon dot eyes, no highlights/gloss, no large circular eyes, no tall ovals. Same relative small eye size as master (around 32 pixels on a 1254 canvas with comparable head scale), adjust placement through head pose only.
- The master tail has a long dark feathered coat and is carried LOW. For this controlled P1 pose set, explicitly keep the tail rooted at the pelvis and pointing back/down to near the ground in every action, NEVER upright, ring-curled or over the back. Keep the same fur length and root connection. This LOW CARRIAGE is a production pose choice, not a verified fixed trait of the real dog. In the stretch the tail can slope down from raised hips; in shaking use a small low lateral flick, not an erect tail.
- Exactly four connected canine limbs total. Use actual joints and a stable support polygon. No detached paws, extra paws, human arms, or an unsupported torso. Far feet may be partially occluded but do not draw extra anatomy.
CANVAS AND SUPPORT RULES:
- Keep the whole dog comfortably in frame, same art scale, no crop and no arbitrary re-centering to the head. Use a common invisible near-contact ground baseline at y=1104 on the 1254 square. Grounded near paws touch that baseline, far paws can be a little higher in perspective, lifted paws must clearly separate. Avoid long cast shadows or marks below the paws.
- Preserve the same paper/charcoal crayon grammar and level of simplicity. No UI, text, labels, props, photorealism, or shiny vector rendering. No horizontal mirroring of the whole character.
This is ONE STATIC key pose, not an animation, real pet observation, or proof of gait frequency. No timing or motion-loop claims. Keep same behavior as image 1 while following the specific action below.
ACTION-SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS:
A single controlled key pose of a relaxed four-beat WALK, not running, jumping or begging. Dog travels toward image-left in a readable three-quarter side view. Body supported horizontally above ground at normal standing height; one near forepaw is lifted and reaching forward with a natural slightly bent elbow, the other forepaw is bearing weight; hind paws make a plausible staggered step. Show exactly four anatomical limbs total, far limbs can partially overlap but no duplicate paws. Head at ordinary walking height, face angled slightly toward camera so both small round dot eyes can be seen. Tail follows its reference design naturally; no new tail shape. Tiny friendly mouth may remain, no added excitement symbols.
If a generic action requirement conflicts with the above continuity rules, retain master P1 identity and low tail carriage.
